facts.value: Bart Paull and Doug Littauer, March 1996

evidence.fact: Spindrift Couloir climbed March 1996 by Bart Paull and Doug Littauer, reported in AAJ the next year; others may have climbed it in the late 1980s.

facts.value: Crux at about three-quarters height: a ~100 ft pitch of near-vertical ice, then steep, often runnelled snow to the exit pitches

evidence.fact: Crux about 3/4 height: 100 ft near-vertical ice pitch leading to steep, often runnelled snow up to the exit pitches.

facts.value: Tops out on the summit ridge well west of the summit; descend northwest by rappels and steep downclimbing to the Big Four-Hall Peak col, rounding a subsidiary SW ridge

evidence.fact: Descent goes northwest via rappels and downclimbing to the Big Four/Hall Peak col; a subsidiary SW ridge must be rounded.

facts.value: Serious winter avalanche hazard below the face; ice-cave collapses at the base have killed visitors

evidence.fact: Signs warn of serious winter avalanche hazard; tourists have been killed at the ice caves at the base of the face.

facts.value: Winter, in condition after a thaw (rain to the summit) followed by a cold snap

evidence.fact: A winter climb, in condition typically after warm rain to the summit followed by a cold snap.

facts.value: Nature trail (nearly wheelchair accessible) from the Big Four picnic area on the Mountain Loop Highway

evidence.fact: Approach follows a nature trail, nearly wheelchair accessible, from the Big Four picnic area on the Mountain Loop Highway.

wa_big_four_mountain_spindrift_couloir.note: mattsea.com shows a grade line reading "IV AI IV" (ambiguous, not recorded). AAJ 1997 article 12199713800 again showed only section boilerplate; cascadeclimbers topic 3583 (second-ascent TR thread) states no figures; skimo.co/spindrift-couloir is a different (Wasatch) Spindrift Couloir. All facts single-source.

evidence.fact: Elevation range listed as 3,480-8,286 ft for Booker Mountain.

facts.value: Cascade Pass Trailhead

evidence.fact: Access: Cascade Pass Trailhead; route up Sahale Arm, into Horseshoe Basin, then a steep rock gully to Booker.

facts.value: From Sahale Glacier east end, descend Sahale Peak south buttress to a snow-free gully at ~6,600 ft, cross Horseshoe Basin, bypass a buttress near 6,600 ft

evidence.fact: Went down Sahale Peak south buttress to snow-free gully at 6600 ft; Horseshoe Basin to 6600 ft buttress bypass.

wa_booker_mountain_south_ridge.note: countryhighpoints trip combined Buckner and Booker in one day (25 mi, 11k ft for both peaks) -- not usable for this route. onehikeaweek distance is round trip, not one-way.

facts.value: Class 4

evidence.fact: Route via Quien Sabe Glacier to east-face ledges is Class 4 on notoriously loose rock, with a rappel descent.

facts.value: 2 rappels with a 60 m rope

evidence.fact: TR of the Southeast Face: a 60 m rope allows for 2 rappels.
Party did the route in 3 pitches plus a final belay along the exposed summit ridge.

facts.value: Small alpine rack up to 2 inches

evidence.fact: Small alpine rack up to 2 inches recommended in the TR.

facts.value: Climb the left side of the Quien Sabe Glacier, pass the bergschrund, unrope at the Boston-Sahale col, follow the exposed ridge, then cross the Boston Glacier to the east-face ledge

evidence.fact: Roped up the Quien Sabe, end-ran the bergschrund, unroped at Boston-Sahale col, along ridge, then onto Boston Glacier and the East Face ledge.

facts.value: NPS backcountry permit required for overnight stays (Boston Basin / Sahale Arm high camps)

evidence.fact: North Cascades NP backcountry/climbing permit required for overnight travel; Boston Basin and Sahale Arm are usual high camps.

facts.value: Boston Basin trailhead: Cascade River Road 21.7 mi from Marblemount, ~3,200 ft, then the abandoned Diamond Mine road

evidence.fact: Shared Boston Basin approach: drive 21.7 mi up Cascade River road to the fork at 3,200 ft, follow abandoned Diamond Mine road 0.75 mi.
Boston Peak elevation given as 8,894 ft.

wa_boston_peak_southeast_face.note: MP 107848161 is the Sahale Peak Quien Sabe route; used only for the shared Boston Basin trailhead. Our stored descent says three rappels; the CascadeClimbers TR says two with a 60 m rope -- conflict, single-source each. trailcatjim (Cascade Pass/East Gully variant) rates the crux steps Class 3-4 but follows a different line.

evidence.fact: Described as technically easy but needing a long round-trip hike (citing Goldman, Washington's Highest Mountains).

wa_blackcap_mountain_scramble.note: Wikipedia (citing Goldman 2004) gives 38 mi round trip and 12,700 ft cumulative gain, but names no trailhead, so not matched to our Slate Pass/Buckskin Ridge approach (stored 8,300 ft / 48.6 km) -- not recorded. walkingplacestogether blackcap-mountain-and-monument-peak is a 2-day, 35 mi two-peak trip (day 1 17.4 mi, +9,544/-4,965 ft hike-in and climb) -- a leg of a multi-peak trip, not used.
